subject: Can I use reshape package where measured variables include numeric  vars and factors?

messages.author: c30fe7796f4303d9
messages.subject: Can I use reshape package where measured variables include numeric  vars and factors?
parts:
Hi

I've got some survey data several hundred records by a couple of
hundred measurements that are either continuous measurements; yes/no;
ratings: low, med, severe; categories: more than three.

The idea of melting and casting data appears to be an ingeneous way to
reorganise data in general but will it work for this type of data
where resonses include a mixture of numeric variables and factors?

More specifically will it work for the 'reshape' package or
alternatives as they currently stand? The data have been carefully
constructed/fixed over a long period and just using codes rather than
labels would defeat the purpose/simplicity of the reshape package.
Currently, the "values" are seen as text and all the numbers
disappear.

Thanks

Cheers
Peter

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Can I use reshape package where measured variables include  numeric vars and factors?
parts:
Hi Peter,

That's something reshape isn't really designed for, mainly because
there are lots of possible output situations where the mingling of
character and numeric data doesn't make sense. One approach to work
around it would be to have two molten data frames, one with only
character data, and one with only numeric data. Depending on what
you're doing with the data, another approach would be to use my new
plyr package (http://had.co.nz/plyr), which doesn't have the same
restrictions on variable type.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Can I use reshape package where measured variables include  numeric vars and factors?
parts: > That's something reshape isn't really designed for, mainly because
> mingling of character and numeric data doesn't make sense.

Well I have to disagree with you on this. If I was still working in
agricultural research I would say this often makes sense but in
medical/social research many outputs/response variables are often
categorical. I take your point though and I realise that it would make
the reshape package messier and involve much more book keeping.

I like the idea of keeping character/factors and numeric variables in
a separate data frames so I'll explore that. meanwhile I've resorted
to cbind, rbind, sort and subscripting which seems the most efficient
- the reshape function (not package) appears to have a massive memory
leak even on fairly small data sets so I've given up on that
temporarily although I'll revisit it and investigate plyr soon

Thanks again!

Cheers
Peter

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Can I use reshape package where measured variables include  numeric vars and factors?
parts: >> That's something reshape isn't really designed for, mainly because

>> mingling of character and numeric data doesn't make sense.
>
> Well I have to disagree with you on this. If I was still working in
> agricultural research I would say this often makes sense but in
> medical/social research many outputs/response variables are often
> categorical. I take your point though and I realise that it would make
> the reshape package messier and involve much more book keeping.

That statement came out rather more provocative than I intended! What
I meant to say is that because columns in R data frames need to be of
the same type, in the presence of mixed types of measured variables
there are many possible outputs from cast that wouldn't produce a
valid R data frame. Additionally, there are very few aggregation
functions that make sense for both numeric and categorical data.
Combined, those two facts mean I couldn't figure out how to make cast
work with both numeric and non-numeric data.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Can I use reshape package where measured variables include  numeric vars and factors?
parts:
Hi Hadley

I didn't take your statement as being too provocative. My guess is
that combining numeric vectors and factors would certainly complicate
things greatly and as you say wouldn't necessarily serve much purpose
in terms of some aggregation functions.

My main aim was to reshape data for analysis and so the basic reshape
function (not in your reshape package) should have done the trick.
Unfortunately I couldn't get it to work without chewing up all
available memory - even when I transfered it to a 6Gb RAM linux box.

I really like the the concept of melting and casting data so I'll
investigate these further as time permits. Its certainly no drama to
keep numerical variables and factors in separate data frames.

Thanks

Cheers
Peter
